title: Traffic operator handbook and rapid fallback protocol (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working handbook for operators who steward progressive traffic changes (canaries, small-batch ABs, staged activations) and need a crisp rapid-fallback protocol when signals cross thresholds. Focus is on human decision flow + machine automation boundary: who does what in the first 15 minutes, 1 hour, and 6 hours after a deviation.

Intended audience:
- Traffic stewards (rotating daily/weekly role)
- Release conductor / oncall SRE
- Product owner for the feature
- Solutions/SE on-call for customer impacts

Glossary (short):
- Steward: primary human responsible for the traffic slice during the window
- Canary slice: initial small percentage of users or cohorts exposed to new model/feature
- Rapid fallback: immediate action that reduces exposure with minimal manual steps (traffic switch, route to previous model, disable feature flag)
- Observation window: configured metric aggregation time (default 5m primary, 1h secondary)

Runbook: first 15 minutes (automated + human triage)
1) Alert fires (automated): threshold breach on primary signal (latency p99 > target OR error spike OR safety signal alert).
   - System posts to #canary-ops Slack and opens a Linear ticket INF-auto-XXXXX.
   - Steward gets paged (rotation list).
2) Steward quick screen (3–5 min):
   - Check Console -> cohort telemetry for the slice. Look at: requests/min, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token cost per request, and safety-rate (moderation hits).
   - Quick context: Has traffic changed (deploy + traffic increase)? Are there infra incidents? (SRE status page).
3) If signal is mild (<= 20% above baseline) and scoped to one cohort, run a focused re-observe: 10 minutes with extended sampling.
4) If signal is severe (> 20% spike, sustained or cross-signal with safety), trigger RAPID FALLBACK.

Rapid fallback checklist (1–3 clicks goal):
- Primary option: route slice to previous model version (Console route rollback).
- Secondary: drop slice to 0% exposure (traffic switch) and flip feature gate to disabled.
- Tertiary (if model-level revert not possible): move slice to lower tier (use Dedicated->Hosted fallback mapping) or divert to a simpler policy (e.g., short-circuit to cached responses).

Who executes what:
- Steward: executes the fallback, annotates the incident in Linear, notifies product and SE.
- SRE: if fallback is traffic-router-related or infra errors, coordinate matrix rollback of infra changes.
- Product: assess user-visible impact and customer notification needs.

Post-fallback: immediate actions (15–60 minutes)
- Capture a snapshot of request traces for the last 30 minutes (Console snapshot tool).
- Export sample inputs/outputs (redact PII) and upload to linked Linear ticket.
- Set a tentative window for re-enable (usually 24–72 hours) and assign an investigation owner.

Investigation and experiment hygiene (1–72 hours)
- First 1–6 hours: triage to narrow causes: prompt/template change, model variant regressions, sequence length distribution, infra noise, or dataset shift.
- If safety or hallucination regressions: run the new examples through validation harness and create an eval job (Optimize).
- Create an isolation replay: replay traffic of failing cohort in a sandboxed environment and run A/B metrics comparisons.

Metrics and signal definitions (what to track every rollout)
- Primary safety signal: percent of responses flagged by content filter OR manual-review false-positive rate on a rolling 1h window.
- Primary performance: p99 latency for the slice (5m and 1h), and success rate (200 OK).
- User-experience proxies: completion length outliers, abrupt stops, and user cancellations (if instrumented).
- Cost guardrail: token-per-completion > 2x baseline triggers caution.
- Statistical checks: use sequential testing heuristics — require 95% CI overlap and minimum sample n per cohort before increasing exposure.

Cohort composition and allocation guidance
- Prefer deterministic cohorts over randomized sampling for early canaries (e.g., internal users, power-users, low-risk countries).
- Micro slices: start at 0.1%–1% for high-risk safety changes; 5%–10% for purely perf optimizations.
- Maintain an exposure ladder: internal -> beta -> regional -> global. Each step requires explicit sign-off from steward + product + SE.

Human-in-the-loop checkpoints and ceremonies
- Preflight checklist (must be green before activation): feature flag toggles defined, expected failure modes documented in ticket, rollback path validated in staging, obs dashboards linked in the ticket.
- Activation ceremony: quick sync (15 min) between steward, product PM, and SE before moving >10% exposure.
- Mid-activation check: steward posts status in channel at 30m and 2h marks with one-line signal summary.

Edge cases and heuristics (notes):
- Oscillation detection: if we see alternating fallback/re-enable within 2h, move to quarantine: pause automated rollups and escalate to SRE/product for manual orchestration.
- Dependent features: if the change touches rerankers or downstream inference, include downstream owners in the preflight and widen the observation matrix.
- Long tail regressions: add a 24h-daylight recheck after full exposure using sampled production traffic for safety signals.

Templates (copy-paste into Linear/Slack)
- Incident opening template (Linear):
  Title: [Canary ALERT] <feature> - <slice> - <primary-signal>
  Body: one-line summary, time, immediate action taken (fallback/route rollback), links to snapshots, expected impact, owner (steward).

- Slack status blurb (channel #canary-ops):
  "[STEWARD] 14:12 UTC: Canary <feature> <slice> -> triggered latency p99 1200ms (> target 800ms). Rapid fallback executed (route -> previous). Impact: ~0.8% of traffic. Investigation assigned to @Ravi. Linear INF-4567."

Open questions / TODOs (work in progress)
- How to encode multi-signal voting in automated rules without exploding false positives? Need agent to combine safety+latency+error signals with weighted thresholds.
- Define a canonical severity matrix mapping compound-signal patterns -> escalation path (pager vs channel vs async ticket).
- Make rapid fallback execution auditable and reversible with a single click in Console (dev ticket filed with infra).

Low-friction improvements we can ship fast
- Add a one-click "snapshot + redact + attach" button in Console to speed sample collection.
- Pre-bake rollback buttons for common fallbacks per feature (model revert / route drop / feature flag off).
- Export steward rota as calendar invites to reduce paging latency.

References and related artifacts:
- Linear: INF-3245 traffic operator rotas (linked above)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim PR#12 (small traffic simulation helpers)
- Confluence draft: Traffic Operator Runbook (internal draft)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider a tiny ML classifier for "likely-safety-regression" that runs on sampled responses during canary (low-cost, high-precision signals only).
- Need to align with Dedicated fallback cost policies (product + finance) so we don't accidentally route expensive traffic to cheaper backend and blow budget.

If you are the steward on duty:
1) Breathe. 2) Read the one-line alert. 3) If uncertain, lean to fallback. 4) Annotate everything and assign investigation owner.

-- end of working draft --
